clue.text: Thought of place in instrumental part

indicators.note: one thing set in another is placed inside it, so the word for place sits within the other piece

blocks.note: the reed is the vibrating part of a woodwind instrument
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone muses about where to place a passage within a piece of instrumental music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental part' suggests a passage of music; here it is the vibrating sliver in a clarinet or oboe mouthpiece, split open to hold the word for place.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed, as in 'thought of' as being so.

clue.text: Decay reported beneath the building

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: rot is decay
beneath means under; in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like these letters

explanation.surface: Rot has been reported in the foundations under the building.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'under' ends with an unvoiced R, so it can stand for the ending UNDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually topped with a dome.

clue.text: Write to address occupied by single retiree

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it inside, so the word for single goes within the form of address

blocks.note: to pen is to write
sir is a respectful form of address
single as a number is one

explanation.surface: Instructions to send a letter to a home where a lone retired person lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner is someone drawing a pension, typically a retired person.

clue.text: Not long retired back to Home Counties

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the abbreviation is read from its end

blocks.note: RET is the standard abbreviation for retired
the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England

explanation.surface: Someone who recently retired moves back to the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, all in England's South East, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech or writing is brief and clipped, so not long.

clue.text: Restraint shown by vicar?

blocks.note: first meaning: the collar a dog wears to be held on a lead
second meaning: the stiff white clerical collar a clergyman wears

explanation.surface: A vicar seems to show admirable self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'restraint' is not self-control but a literal piece of kit for an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The same phrase names both a pet's neckband for leading it and the white band of a clergyman's dress.

clue.text: Hide private note

blocks.note: something private is secret
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone tucks away a confidential message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a single musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, an older sense alongside the biological one.

clue.text: Follow up apologetic expression with loud joke

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the expression runs backwards

blocks.note: oops is what you say when apologising for a slip
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: After an embarrassed apology, someone tells a noisy joke to cover it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a light-hearted parody or hoax, a kind of joke.

clue.text: Measure pieces of wood for cabinets

blocks.note: a cup is a unit of measure in cooking
boards are flat lengths of timber

explanation.surface: A carpenter measures up timber to build cabinets.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupboards are storage cabinets with doors and shelves.

clue.text: The best of English literature came at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only of the word it follows

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lit is the short form of literature
the final letter of came

explanation.surface: A remark that the finest English writing arrived only late on.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the select few.

clue.text: Top of old meter damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ex- means former, old
the five letters of meter rearranged

explanation.surface: The top part of an antique gauge has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as a noun for the meter's lid; as the definition it is an adjective meaning utmost.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and top both mean at the utmost limit, as in top speed or extreme speed.

clue.text: Meaning detected in written order

indicators.note: something detected in a phrase was there all along, lying across its words

blocks.note: the gist or general sense of something
runs across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Something significant is spotted within a written command.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one definition here; the rest of the clue hides the word across two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a document is its general drift or purport.

clue.text: Right to indicate concession

blocks.note: right in the sense of good, proper
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: Someone claims an entitlement to signal a compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'good point' concedes that the other side of an argument has made a valid remark.

clue.text: Play with racket

blocks.note: surface reading: messing about with a tennis or squash racket
setter's reading: a stage play whose title means din, the racket heard from the wings

explanation.walkthrough: Michael Frayn's farce takes its title from the stage direction for sounds made offstage, so the play itself is a noisy one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a well-known comic play whose title is a theatre term for offstage sound effects.

clue.text: Large instruments ring out to the end

indicators.note: something out is gone, so the ring-shaped letter is dropped from the instruments
the end of a word is its final letter alone

blocks.note: oboes are woodwind instruments
a ring is O-shaped
the last letter of the

explanation.surface: Big instruments resound right to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring out' reads as resound; here it means take an O out of OBOES. 'The end' is the last letter of the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, a stronger sense of large.

clue.text: Bother! The sound system won't start

indicators.note: something that won't start is missing its beginning, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: Tannoy is a brand of public-address system, used generically in Britain

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry when the PA system fails to come on.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is the British name for a public-address loudspeaker system, as in stations and schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to irritate or pester them.

clue.text: Time for a song?

blocks.note: first meaning: the day before today
second meaning: a famous Beatles song

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is the moment to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yesterday' is one of the most covered songs ever, written by Paul McCartney.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a point in time, the previous day, and is also the title of a classic Beatles ballad.

clue.text: Generous man left to get prong for rake

indicators.note: the man has left, so his name departs from the word for generous

blocks.note: liberal means generous, open-handed
Al is a man's name
a tine is a prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A generous man goes off to fetch a prong for his garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool, fitting prong; it means a dissolute man. 'Left' reads as the direction L, but signals departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a debauched pleasure-seeker, which is just what a libertine is.

clue.text: Old chap's heading for depression and heart trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of the organ are stirred up

blocks.note: a bowl is a hollow or depression in land
the letters of heart rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man is on course for low mood and cardiac problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' here means headwear: a bowler hat is a hard round felt hat, the traditional City gent's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowler is the hat that sits on an old-fashioned English gentleman's head, a playful sense of heading.

clue.text: Secretly finds home with soldier

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: Someone quietly tracks down a house where a soldier lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in private means doing it away from others, which is secretly.

clue.text: Finding rocks slippery, team has to turn round

indicators.note: slippery things slide about and won't stay put, so these letters shift

blocks.note: the letters of rocks rearranged
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A climbing party, struggling on slippery rocks, has to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' reads as retreat; as the definition it means to spiral.
explanation.definitionFit: To corkscrew is to move in a spiral, twisting round like the tool.

clue.text: Fancy collar wrapped round flowery section

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged
a thing wrapped around another encloses it, so the scrambled collar goes outside

blocks.note: the letters of collar rearranged
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A decorative collar wrapped around a floral-patterned piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like part of 'wrapped round'; it gives the O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the whorl of petals forming the showy part of a flower.

clue.text: Get change from purse for fine

indicators.note: making change rearranges what is there, so these letters come out in another order

blocks.note: the letters of purse rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes coins from a purse to pay a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like the penalty you pay; it is the adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Super and fine are both informal words of approval meaning very good.

clue.text: Softens when one abandons story in tears

indicators.note: the one abandons the word, so a single I is taken away
something in another sits inside it, so what remains of the story goes within

blocks.note: rents are rips or tears
I is the Roman numeral one
a story can be a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: Someone's heart melts when a sad tale is dropped and they are left crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping; it means rips (rhymes with 'cares').
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relents softens their stance and becomes less severe.

clue.text: Mountain range is clear example, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the abbreviation runs backwards

blocks.note: to rid is to clear
e.g. is short for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Looking back, a mountain range is a clear case of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow stretch of high ground, a line of mountain crests.

clue.text: Dance made up of two circles

blocks.note: a disc is one circle and O is another

explanation.surface: A dance consisting of two rings of dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: The two circles are DISC and the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club for dancing to recorded music.

clue.text: Routine step on road for students

blocks.note: to tread is to step
the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as MI
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A step out onto the road where learner drivers practise.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a monotonous routine, from the wheel walked by prisoners or animals.

clue.text: Raise it with the amount once taxed

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to increase a sum together with what was once taxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid as a tax to the church in former times.

clue.text: First performance of complex duet without book

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so its letters are mixed
without in its old sense means outside, so the scrambled duet surrounds the book

blocks.note: the letters of duet rearranged
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A tricky duet is premiered without a score to read from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is someone's first public appearance or performance.

clue.text: Go on to abandon final

blocks.note: to last is to go on, continue
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: An urge to carry on rather than give up on the final.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt, from the last line of defence.

clue.text: Support given to fashionable intellectual

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Backing is offered to a trendy thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' sounds like backing; it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain is informally a very clever person, an intellectual.

clue.text: A refusal to deny unorthodox painkiller

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
no is a refusal
the letters of deny rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to rule out an alternative pain remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a drug or treatment that relieves pain.

clue.text: In tunnel's outer confines, animal lurches

indicators.note: the outer confines of a word are its boundary letters at each end
something in confines is held inside them, so the animal sits within

blocks.note: the first and last letters of tunnel's
an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal staggers about within the walls of a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, much as one lurches.
